chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn Ayyub, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), who said:

While Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) was upon the pulpit, a snake approached from the direction of one of the doors of the masjid. The people intended to kill it, so Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) sent word that they should refrain, and they refrained. The snake came gliding until it reached the pulpit, then it raised itself and greeted Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام), so Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) indicated to it to stand until he finished his sermon.

When he had finished his sermon, he turned to it and said, 'Who are you?' It said, 'Amr ibn Uthman, your khalifah over the jinn. My father died and instructed me to come to you and seek your view. I have come to you, O Amir al-Mu'minin, so what do you command me with, and what do you see?'

Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) said to him, 'I advise you to have taqwa of Allah, and to return and assume the place of your father among the jinn, for you are my khalifah over them.' He said: So Amr bade farewell to Amir al-Mu'minin and departed, and he was his khalifah over the jinn.
So I said to him, 'May I be made your ransom, does Amr come to you, and is that obligatory upon him?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Ali (عليه السلام), addressed here as the authoritative leader
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: the jinn, the unseen beings over whom the visitor said he had been appointed
key_terms.الْمِنْبَرِ: the pulpit from which the sermon was being delivered
key_terms.تَقْوَى اللَّهِ: God-consciousness and piety, the core instruction given by the Imam
key_terms.ثُعْبَانٌ: a snake, the form in which the visitor appeared
key_terms.خَلِيفَتُكَ: your khalifah, meaning your appointed representative or deputy
key_terms.خُطْبَتِهِ: his sermon, which the Imam completed before addressing the visitor

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the authority of Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) over the jinn?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that a representative from the jinn came to Amir al-Mu'minin (عليه السلام) in the form of a snake and sought his instruction regarding succession among the jinn. It highlights his authority being recognized beyond humankind and shows that his counsel to that representative centered on taqwa and rightful leadership. The report also indicates that the jinn would come to the Imams (عليهم السلام) for guidance in the affairs of their religion.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Ibrahim Bin Hashim, from Amro Bin Usman, from Ibrahim Bin Ayoub, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘While Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was upon the Pulpit, a snake came over from the direction of a door from the doors of the Masjid. So the people thought of killing it, but Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> sent a message that they should refrain. So they refrained, and the snake glided until it ended up to the Pulpit, and stood elongated and greeted upon Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>. But, Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> gestured towards it that it should pause until he<sup>asws</sup> is free from his<sup>asws</sup> sermon.

And when he<sup>asws</sup> was free from his<sup>asws</sup> sermon, he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards it and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Who are you?’ So it said, ‘Amro Bin Usman, your Caliph upon the Jinn, and that my father died and bequeathed me that I should come over to you and find out your<sup>asws</sup> view, and so I have come to you, O Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>! So what are you<sup>asws</sup> ordering me with, and what is your<sup>asws</sup> view?’

So Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said to it: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> command you with the fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and when you leave, so you should stand in the place of your father among the Jinn, for you are (now) my<sup>asws</sup> Caliph upon them’. So Amro bade farewell to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> and left, and he was his<sup>asws</sup> Caliph upon the Jinn’.
So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! So does Amro come to you, and is that An Obligation upon him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Muhammad have narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman from Ibrahim ibn Ayyub from ‘Amr ibn Shimr from Jabir from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Once when Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) was on the pulpit a serpent entered from one of the doors of the mosque. People wanted to kill him. Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) asked them to leave him alone. They left him alone. The serpent began to crawl to the pulpit. He stretched and saluted to Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.). Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) made a gesture to him to wait until the sermon is completed.

When the sermon was completed he came to him and said, “Who are you?” He said, “I am ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman, your deputy among the Jinns. My father has died and he has asked me in his will to come to you and find out your instructions and that is why I am here. What do you command me to do and what do you see.”

Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) said, “I ask you to be pious before Allah and go back and act as the successor of your father among the Jinns. I appoint you as my deputy over them.” The narrator has said that ‘Amr then said farewell to Amir al-Mu’minin (a.s.) and left as his deputy over the Jinns.
I asked The Imam (a.s.), may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, does ‘Amr fulfill that obligation on him?” He said, “Yes, he does so.”
